gloss: mass resignation; en bloc resignation (of a cabinet)

definitions.gloss: mass resignation; en bloc resignation (especially of a cabinet)
definitions.explanation: The simultaneous resignation of all members of a body — most often a national cabinet, but also a corporate board or committee. Often takes する.

examples.japanese: {内閣|ないかく}が{総辞職|そうじしょく}した。
{首相|しゅしょう}は{総辞職|そうじしょく}を{表明|ひょうめい}した。
examples.english: The prime minister announced the cabinet's en bloc resignation.

examples.japanese: {選挙|せんきょ}での{大敗|たいはい}を{受|う}けて{内閣|ないかく}は{総辞職|そうじしょく}を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた。
examples.english: Following a crushing defeat in the election, the cabinet was forced to resign en masse.

notes:
Compound of {総|そう} (whole, all) + {辞職|じしょく} (resignation). Most commonly refers to the formal en bloc resignation of the Japanese cabinet — a constitutional event that occurs after a major election loss or a vote of no confidence. Often used with する.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {内閣|ないかく}{総辞職|そうじしょく}: cabinet en bloc resignation (a fixed term)
- {総辞職|そうじしょく}する: to resign en masse
- {総辞職|そうじしょく}に{追|お}い{込|こ}まれる: to be driven to mass resignation
- {総辞職|そうじしょく}を{表明|ひょうめい}する: to announce mass resignation

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {辞職|じしょく}: resignation — a single person resigning a post
- {退陣|たいじん}: stepping down — often used for a leader leaving office, with no implication of bringing the whole team down
- {解散|かいさん}: dissolution — used for the Diet/parliament, not the cabinet
